# Does a given Swoole git ref's official composer.json `php` constraint admit the running
# PHP? Returns 0 (yes / undeterminable) or 1 (explicitly excluded). Parses the simple
# ">=X.Y" + optional "<A.B" forms Swoole uses (e.g. ">=8.2 <8.6", ">=8.1 <8.5").
swoole_ref_supports_php() {
    local ref="$1" php_ver="$2"
    local pvid; pvid="$(echo "$php_ver"100+$2}')"
    local constraint
    constraint="$(curl -fsSL "https://rle/swoole-src/${ref}/composer.json" 2>/dev/
null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"php"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    [ -z "$constraint" ] && return 0   # offline / unknown -> do not block
    local lo hi
    lo="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '>=?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    hi="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '<[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'   | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    if [ -n "$lo" ]; then
        local loid; loid="$(echo "$lo" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -lt "$loid" ] && return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "$hi" ]; then
        local hiid; hiid="$(echo "$hi" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -ge "$hiid" ] && return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Select the Swoole build ref for the rlable version" rather
# than trust a possibly-stale hardcoded tag:
#   1. $SWOOLE_BUILD_REF if set (explicit override).
#   2. the latest STABLE GitHub release, IF its composer.json admits this PHP.
#   3. the provided known-good pin, IF it admits this PHP.
#   4. master (last resort), with a warning.
# Prints the chosen ref on stdout (diagnostics go to stderr).
select_swoole_build_ref() {
    local php_ver="$1" pin="$2"
    if [ -n "${SWOOLE_BUILD_REF:-}" ]; then
        echo "$SWOOLE_BUILD_REF"; return 0
    fi
    local latest
    latest="$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/swoole/swoole-src/releases/latest" 2>/dev/null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    if printf '%s' "$latest" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' && swoole_ref_supports_php "$latest" "$php_
ver"; then
        echo "$latest"; return 0
    fi
    if swoole_ref_supports_php "$pin" "$php_ver"; then
        echo "$pin"; return 0
    fi
    echo "[WARN] No tagged Swoole release admits PHP ${php_ver}; falling back to master" >&2
    echo "master"
}

# Initialize global temporary directory.
# NOTE: /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias for /var/tmp that exists only as a symlink on
# some RPM distros; on Debian/Ubuntu/Kali it is absent, so clones/builds under it failed
# with "Permission denied". Use $TMPDIR when set, else /var/tmp -- persistent and
# disk-backed (good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp) and world-writable
# + sticky on every Debian-family system, so the invoking non-root user can create build
# dirs here. Export GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR to override.
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}}"
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR%/}"
# Initialize the global temporary directory base.
# It MUST be writable by the invoking (non-root) user, because scripts clone/build here
# as the user (then `make install` as root). Pitfalls this resolver defends against:
#   * /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias n/Ubuntu/Kali; worse,
#     an older revision of this file created it as root:root 0755 (unwritable), and a
#     long-running menu may still EXPOnto child scripts.
#   * So a stale/unwritable INHERITED value must be SKIPPED, not preserved -- using
#     "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-...}" alone would keep the bad /usr/tmp.
# Resolution order (first that is a WRITABLE dir, or can be created writable, wins):
#   exported GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR, $TMPDIR, /var/tmp, /tmp. /var/tmp is preferred (persistent +
#   disk-backed -> good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp).
__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common() {
    local c
    for c in "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-}" "${TMPDIR:-}" /var/tmp /tmp; do
        [ -z "$c" ] && continue
        c="${c%/}"
        if { [ -d "$c" ] || mkdir -p "$c" 2>/dev/null; } && [ -w "$c" ]; then
            echo "$c"; return 0
        fi
    done
    echo /tmp
}
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="$(__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common)"
unset -f __resolve_global_temp_dir_fro

# Ensure global temporary directory exMISSING -- never
# chmod an existing system temp dir, which would clobber its 1777 sticky permissions.
if [ ! -d "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Creating global temporary directory: $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Function to create script-specific temporary directory (restricted to $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR/<script_name>)
create_script_temp_dir() {
    local script_name="$1"

ensure_php_symlink() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP 8.5 symlink exists...${NC}"
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP ${PHP_VERSION} is the default php...${NC}"

    if [ ! -f "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink missing or incorrect, fixing...${NC}"
    if [ ! -x "$PHP_BIN" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} binary not found at $PHP_BIN${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php85_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
        return 1
    fi

        if [ -f "/usr/bin/php8.5" ]; then
            # Register php8.5 (idempotent) without wiping other PHP alternatives.
            # --remove-all would destroy every registered php alternative on rerun.
            $USE_SUDO update-alternativ /usr/bin/php8.5 84
            $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php /usr/bin/php8.5
            echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 binary not found at /usr/bin/php8.5${NC}"
            echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php84_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink already exists${NC}"
    # 1) /usr/bin/php via update-alternatives -- SAME priority as step 31 (shared
    #    PHP_ALT_PRIORITY) so re-running this step never lowers the default 31 set.
    #    No --remove-all (that would wipe other registered php alternatives).
    if [ ! -e "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/php php "$PHP_BIN" "$PHP_ALT_PRIORITY"
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php "$PHP_BIN"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} set as default (priority ${PHP_ALT_PRIORITY})${NC}"
    fi

    if /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX r/bin/php${NC}"
    # 2) The canonical entrypoint link that step 31 CREATES and step 34 CONSUMES.
    #    32 previously only checked /ushile this contract
    #    link was broken. Keep it in sync here too.
    if [ "$(readlink -f "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" 2>/dev/null)" != "$(readlink -f "$PHP_BIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TARGET_LINK_PATH")"
        $USE_SUDO ln -sf "$PHP_BIN" "$TARGET_LINK_PATH"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX Linked $TARGET_LINK_PATH -> $PHP_BIN${NC}"
    fi

    if "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} available at $TARGET_LINK_PATH and /usr/bin/php${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to set PHP 8.5 as default${NC}"
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to make PHP ${PHP_VERSION} the default${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}

The unavoidable catch: Kali (tracking Debian sid/forky) already moved to libxml2 2.15 / .so.16. Sury's newest build (trixie) still links libxml2.so.2. php8.5-cli itself depends on libxml2 (libxml is core, non-disableable PHP), so no Sury PHP 8.5 can install or run on Kali 2026.2 without a libxml2.so.2 present. # COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivativ already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Pro unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (present on such systems) and co-installs cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or the distro still ships a real `libxml2` candidate.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior sge is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2
    echo "[libxml2-compat]   it ships only the newer libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16." >&2

    case "${PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM:-1}" in
        0|false|no|off)
            echo "[libxml2-compat] PHP_-> NOT installing the compat lib." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] The PHP 8.5 install will fail until libxml2.so.2 is provided." >&2
            echo "[libxml2-compat] Re-rIM=1 (default) to auto-install it." >&2
            return 0
            ;;
    esac

    local arch; arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture 2>/dev/null || echo amd64)"
    local idx_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/dists/${php_codename}/main/binary-${arch}/Packages.gz"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Resolving Debian ${php_codename} libxml2 (.so.2) compat package..." >&2

    local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp -d 2>/dev/null || echo "/tmp/libxml2compat.$$")"
    mkdir -p "$tmp"
    local idx="$tmp/Packages.gz"
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$idx" "$idx_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: could not fetch Debian package index ($idx_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    # Filename: of the binary package named exactly 'libxml2' (the .so.2 one). The
    # trailing \n in the regex preventsxml2-dev / etc.
    local fname
    fname="$(zcat "$idx" 2>/dev/null \
        | awk 'BEGIN{RS="";ORS="\n\n"} /(^|\n)Package: libxml2\n/' \
        | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
    if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: Debian ${php_codename} has no 'libxml2' (.so.2) package." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    local deb_url="http://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}"
    local deb="$tmp/libxml2-compat.deb"
    echo "[libxml2-compat] Downloading ${deb_url}" >&2
    if ! curl -fsSL -o "$deb" "$deb_url"; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] ERROR: download failed ($deb_url)." >&2
        rm -rf "$tmp"; return 1
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] Installing compat libxml2 (.so.2) alongside libxml2-16..." >&2
    if ! $USE_SUDO dpkg -i "$deb"; then
        # Pull any missing deps from th1g normally present).
        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxml2.so.2 now available (Debian ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
}

# Add PHP repository (Ubuntu/Debian) with automatic backup and restore
# Ubuntu: uses ppa.launchpadcontent.net and Launchpad PPA signing key (avoids certificate mismatch with ppa.lau
nchpad.net)
# Debian: uses packages.sury.org and Sury key

# COMMON REPOSITORY MANAGEMENT FUNCTIONS
# ============================================================================

# Bridge the libxml2 SONAME gap so Sury PHP 8.5 can install AND run on bleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling).
# Bridge SONAME/library gaps so Sury PHbleeding-edge
# Debian derivatives (e.g. Kali rolling) that have moved ahead of the suite Sury
# builds against.
#
# Sury's php8.5-cli / php8.5-xml depend on the historic `libxml2` package, which
# ships libxml2.so.2. Rolling derivatives that track Debian sid have already moved to
# libxml2 2.15 (package `libxml2-16`, soname libxml2.so.16) and dropped the old
# `libxml2` package with no virtual Provides -- so the dependency is unsatisfiable
# and, even if force-installed, the PHP binary (linked against .so.2) would fail to
# load. libxml2 is core, non-disableable PHP, so this blocks PHP entirely.
# Sury's php8.5-* packages (built for Debian <codename>) depend on that suite's library
# versions -- e.g. php8.5-cli/xml -> `libxml2` (libxml2.so.2), php8.5-intl -> `libicu76`.
# Rolling derivatives that track Debian sid have already bumped those SONAMEs (libxml2
# 2.15 -> package libxml2-16 / libxml2.so.16; ICU 76 -> libicu77+) and DROPPED the old
# package names with no virtual Provides, so the dependency is unsatisfiable and the
# extension binaries (linked against the old soname) would not load. libxml2 is core,
# non-disableable PHP, so a missing libxml2 blocks PHP entirely.
#
# When the gap is detected, install Debian's `libxml2` (.so.2) compat package for the
# resolved Sury codename (the suite Sury built against, so the ABI matches). It depends
# only on libc6/liblzma5/zlib1g (presentalls cleanly next
# to libxml2-16 (different package name, different .so files). Idempotent; a no-op when
# libxml2.so.2 is already present or thlibxml2` candidate.
# For each library dependency of the REQUESTED php packages that is unsatisfiable on
# this host, install Debian <codename>'s build of that exact library (the suite Sury
# built against -> ABI match). Such libs are SONAME-versioned, so they co-install
# cleanly next to the distro's newer version (different package name + different .so).
# Only libs that the requested php packages actually need AND that the host lacks AND
# that Debian publishes are touched -- never a blanket pull (so e.g. libsnmp40t64 for
# php8.5-snmp is left alone when that extension is not requested). Idempotent: a no-op
# once the libs are installed or the distro already satisfies them.
#
# Opt out with PHP_LIBXML2_COMPAT_SHIM=0 -- then a clear gap message is printed and the
# caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly instead of silently mixing in a lib.
ensure_php_libxml2_compat_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"     # ubuntu | debian
    local php_codename="$2"   # resolved repo codename (e.g. trixie)
# Security: each .deb is fetched over HTTPS and verified against the SHA256 in the same
# Packages index stanza before it is installed as root; a mismatch discards the file.
#
# Opt out with PHP_COMPAT_SHIM=0 (legacIM=0) -- then a
# clear gap report is printed and the caller's PHP install is left to fail loudly
# instead of silently mixing in a lib.
#
# Args: <vendor: ubuntu|debian> <codename> <space-separated php package list>
ensure_php_compat_libs_from_apt_repository_manager() {
    local php_vendor="$1"
    local php_codename="$2"
    local php_pkgs="$3"

    # Only the Debian/Sury path is affected; Ubuntu's ondrej PPA tracks Ubuntu libs.
    [ "$php_vendor" = "debian" ] || return 0
    [ -n "${php_pkgs// /}" ] || return 0

    # Already satisfiable? Either the distro offers a real `libxml2` candidate, the
    # .so.2 is already on disk (prior shim / leftover), or the package is installed.
    local cand
    cand="$(apt-cache policy libxml2 2>/dev/null | awk '/Candidate:/{print $2}')"
    if [ -n "$cand" ] && [ "$cand" != "(none)" ]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        return 0
    fi
    if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' libxml2 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then
        return 0
    fi

    echo "[libxml2-compat] This distro has no 'libxml2' (libxml2.so.2) package that Sury PHP 8.5 needs;" >&2

        gaps="$gaps $lib"

        $USE_SUDO apt-get -f install -y 2>/dev/null || true
    local debs="" missing="" stanza fname exp_sha got_sha out
    for lib in $gaps; do
        stanza="$(zcat "$deb_idx" 2>/dev/null | awk -v RS='' -v p="$lib" 'index($0 "\n", "Package: " p "\n")==1
' | head -c 200000)"
        fname="$(printf '%s\n' "$stanza" | sed -n 's/^Filename: //p' | head -n1)"
        exp_sha="$(printf '%s\n' "$stanza" | sed -n 's/^SHA256: //p' | head -n1)"
        if [ -z "$fname" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] NOTE: Debian ${php_codename} has no '${lib}' package; cannot shim it." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        out="$tmp/${lib}.deb"
        echo "[php-compat] Fetching ${lib} <- https://deb.debian.org/debian/${fname}" >&2
        if ! curl -fsSL -o "$out" "httpname}"; then
            echo "[php-compat] WARNING: download failed for ${lib}." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        if [ -z "$exp_sha" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] ERROR: no SHA256 in index for ${lib}; refusing to install unverified .deb." >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        got_sha="$(sha256sum "$out" 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')"
        if [ "$got_sha" != "$exp_sha" ]; then
            echo "[php-compat] ERROR: SHA256 mismatch for ${lib} (want ${exp_sha}, got ${got_sha}); discarding.
" >&2
            missing="$missing $lib"; continue
        fi
        debs="$debs $out"
    done

    # 5) Install all verified compat libs at once (so any inter-deps resolve together),
    #    non-interactively, keeping exioving packages to
    #    "fix" the transaction. Diagnostics are NOT swallowed.
    if [ -n "${debs// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] Installing verified compat libs alongside the distro's newer versions..." >&2
        if ! $USE_SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive dpkg -i --force-confold $debs; then
            $USE_SUDO env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -f install -y \
                -o APT::Get::Remove=false -o Dpkg::Options::=--force-confold || true
        fi
    fi

    # 6) Verify outcome loudly. A lib that is unshimmable (no Debian package / failed
    #    verify) is reported but not treated as the whole step failing.
    local still_missing=""
    for lib in $gaps; do
        if dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$lib" 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'install ok installed'; then continue; fi
        case " $missing " in *" $lib "*) continue ;; esac
        still_missing="$still_missing $lib"
    done

    rm -rf "$tmp"

    if ldconfig -p 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'libxml2\.so\.2'; then
        echo "[libxml2-compat] OK: libxn ${php_codename} compat lib)." >&2
        return 0
    if [ -n "${still_missing// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] WARNING: compat libs still not installed:${still_missing} -- the PHP packages needin
g them will fail." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    echo "[libxml2-compat] WARNING: libxml2.so.2 still absent after shim; PHP install may fail." >&2
    return 1
    if [ -n "${missing// /}" ]; then
        echo "[php-compat] NOTE: no verified Debian compat for:${missing} (only extensions needing them are aff
ected)." >&2
    fi
    echo "[php-compat] OK: compat libraries provided for ${php_codename}." >&2
    return 0
}

# Initialize global temporary directory
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="/usr/tmp"
# Initialize global temporary directory.
# NOTE: /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias for /var/tmp that exists only as a symlink on
# some RPM distros; on Debian/Ubuntu/Kuilds under it failed
# with "Permission denied". Use $TMPDIR when set, else /var/tmp -- persistent and
# disk-backed (good for large source b) and world-writable
# + sticky on every Debian-family system, so the invoking non-root user can create build
# dirs here. Export GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR to override.
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}}"
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR%/}"

# Ensure global temporary directory exists
# Ensure global temporary directory exists. Only create/chmod when MISSING -- never
# chmod an existing system temp dir, which would clobber its 1777 sticky permissions.
if [ ! -d "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Creating global temporary directory: $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    $USE_SUDO chmod 755 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Does a given Swoole git ref's official composer.json `php` constraint admit the running
# PHP? Returns 0 (yes / undeterminable) or 1 (explicitly excluded). Parses the simple
# ">=X.Y" + optional "<A.B" forms Swoole uses (e.g. ">=8.2 <8.6", ">=8.1 <8.5").
swoole_ref_supports_php() {
    local ref="$1" php_ver="$2"
    local pvid; pvid="$(echo "$php_ver"100+$2}')"
    local constraint
    constraint="$(curl -fsSL "https://rle/swoole-src/${ref}/composer.json" 2>/dev/
null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"php"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    [ -z "$constraint" ] && return 0   # offline / unknown -> do not block
    local lo hi
    lo="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '>=?[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    hi="$(printf '%s' "$constraint" | grep -oE '<[[:space:]]*[0-9]+\.[0-9]+'   | head -n1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[
0-9]+')"
    if [ -n "$lo" ]; then
        local loid; loid="$(echo "$lo" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -lt "$loid" ] && return 1
    fi
    if [ -n "$hi" ]; then
        local hiid; hiid="$(echo "$hi" | awk -F. '{printf "%d", $1*100+$2}')"
        [ "$pvid" -ge "$hiid" ] && return 1
    fi
    return 0
}

# Select the Swoole build ref for the rlable version" rather
# than trust a possibly-stale hardcoded tag:
#   1. $SWOOLE_BUILD_REF if set (explicit override).
#   2. the latest STABLE GitHub release, IF its composer.json admits this PHP.
#   3. the provided known-good pin, IF it admits this PHP.
#   4. master (last resort), with a warning.
# Prints the chosen ref on stdout (diagnostics go to stderr).
select_swoole_build_ref() {
    local php_ver="$1" pin="$2"
    if [ -n "${SWOOLE_BUILD_REF:-}" ]; then
        echo "$SWOOLE_BUILD_REF"; return 0
    fi
    local latest
    latest="$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/swoole/swoole-src/releases/latest" 2>/dev/null \
        | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
    if printf '%s' "$latest" | grep -qE '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' && swoole_ref_supports_php "$latest" "$php_
ver"; then
        echo "$latest"; return 0
    fi
    if swoole_ref_supports_php "$pin" "$php_ver"; then
        echo "$pin"; return 0
    fi
    echo "[WARN] No tagged Swoole release admits PHP ${php_ver}; falling back to master" >&2
    echo "master"
}

# Initialize global temporary directory.
# NOTE: /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias for /var/tmp that exists only as a symlink on
# some RPM distros; on Debian/Ubuntu/Kali it is absent, so clones/builds under it failed
# with "Permission denied". Use $TMPDIR when set, else /var/tmp -- persistent and
# disk-backed (good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp) and world-writable
# + sticky on every Debian-family system, so the invoking non-root user can create build
# dirs here. Export GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR to override.
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/var/tmp}}"
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR%/}"
# Initialize the global temporary directory base.
# It MUST be writable by the invoking (non-root) user, because scripts clone/build here
# as the user (then `make install` as root). Pitfalls this resolver defends against:
#   * /usr/tmp is a legacy SysV alias n/Ubuntu/Kali; worse,
#     an older revision of this file created it as root:root 0755 (unwritable), and a
#     long-running menu may still EXPOnto child scripts.
#   * So a stale/unwritable INHERITED value must be SKIPPED, not preserved -- using
#     "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-...}" alone would keep the bad /usr/tmp.
# Resolution order (first that is a WRITABLE dir, or can be created writable, wins):
#   exported GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR, $TMPDIR, /var/tmp, /tmp. /var/tmp is preferred (persistent +
#   disk-backed -> good for large source builds, unlike RAM-backed /tmp).
__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common() {
    local c
    for c in "${GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR:-}" "${TMPDIR:-}" /var/tmp /tmp; do
        [ -z "$c" ] && continue
        c="${c%/}"
        if { [ -d "$c" ] || mkdir -p "$c" 2>/dev/null; } && [ -w "$c" ]; then
            echo "$c"; return 0
        fi
    done
    echo /tmp
}
GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR="$(__resolve_global_temp_dir_from_gvar_common)"
unset -f __resolve_global_temp_dir_fro

# Ensure global temporary directory exMISSING -- never
# chmod an existing system temp dir, which would clobber its 1777 sticky permissions.
if [ ! -d "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" ]; then
    echo "Creating global temporary directory: $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR"
    chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || $USE_SUDO chmod 1777 "$GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true
fi

# Function to create script-specific temporary directory (restricted to $GLOBAL_TEMP_DIR/<script_name>)

    local script_name="$1"

ensure_php_symlink() {
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP 8.5 symlink exists...${NC}"
    echo -e "${BLUE}$SCRIPT_INDEX Ensuring PHP ${PHP_VERSION} is the default php...${NC}"

    if [ ! -f "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink missing or incorrect, fixing...${NC}"
    if [ ! -x "$PHP_BIN" ]; then
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} binary not found at $PHP_BIN${NC}"
        echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php85_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
        return 1
    fi

        if [ -f "/usr/bin/php8.5" ]; then
            # Register php8.5 (idempotent) without wiping other PHP alternatives.
            # --remove-all would destroy every registered php alternative on rerun.
            $USE_SUDO update-alternativ /usr/bin/php8.5 84
            $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php /usr/bin/php8.5
            echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INC}"
        else
            echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 binary not found at /usr/bin/php8.5${NC}"
            echo -e "${YELLOW}$SCRIPT_INDEX Please run 31_ensure_php84_intelligent.sh first${NC}"
            return 1
        fi
    else
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP 8.5 symlink already exists${NC}"
    # 1) /usr/bin/php via update-alternatives -- SAME priority as step 31 (shared
    #    PHP_ALT_PRIORITY) so re-running this step never lowers the default 31 set.
    #    No --remove-all (that would wipe other registered php alternatives).
    if [ ! -e "/usr/bin/php" ] || ! /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/php php "$PHP_BIN" "$PHP_ALT_PRIORITY"
        $USE_SUDO update-alternatives --set php "$PHP_BIN"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} set as default (priority ${PHP_ALT_PRIORITY})${NC}"
    fi

    if /usr/bin/php -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP 8.5"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX r/bin/php${NC}"
    # 2) The canonical entrypoint link that step 31 CREATES and step 34 CONSUMES.
    #    32 previously only checked /ushile this contract
    #    link was broken. Keep it in sync here too.
    if [ "$(readlink -f "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" 2>/dev/null)" != "$(readlink -f "$PHP_BIN" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        $USE_SUDO mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TARGET_LINK_PATH")"
        $USE_SUDO ln -sf "$PHP_BIN" "$TARGET_LINK_PATH"
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX Linked $TARGET_LINK_PATH -> $PHP_BIN${NC}"
    fi

    if "$TARGET_LINK_PATH" -v 2>/dev/null | grep -q "PHP ${PHP_VERSION}"; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}$SCRIPT_INDEX PHP ${PHP_VERSION} available at $TARGET_LINK_PATH and /usr/bin/php${NC}"
        return 0
    else
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to set PHP 8.5 as default${NC}"
        echo -e "${RED}$SCRIPT_INDEX Failed to make PHP ${PHP_VERSION} the default${NC}"
        return 1
    fi
}
